en.html:
Morning came, and the rain started again. The black-gray clouds evidently found the sky over Kamakura extremely comfortable. They had vacated it for one night only. Now they were back with their whole weight settled in, as if this was their ancestral property.

Water dripped from the rim of my umbrella onto the back of my hand. Terribly cold.

en.html:
This exchange with Muramasa was the same argument I had conducted with myself hundreds, thousands of times through the night. Only the second voice was coming from outside now. I knew. What I had to do, I knew perfectly well.

A town, a village, any gathering of people: it appeared without warning and annihilated them. The Tempest. Weather made of slaughter. The Silver Star. Modern Yamato's nightmare, and ending it was my work.

Because nobody else could do it.
Because my foster mother had entrusted that wish to me.
Because that was my sister.

Whatever I had to trample, I had to go through with it.

As I had been doing. Two years of crushing lives beneath iron boots. That was the road behind me.

The road ahead would be the same.
Today also.

Ichijou Ayane, waiting at Ennoji—her also—

en.html:
The tsurugi moving under cover nearby was sending me a silent stare. Even without a word, she was managing to be a nuisance. I ignored it and got up.

This body, which I had known so well, had become unreasonably heavy. Relax my hold on it and the knees would begin shaking.

The weight was not body weight. Something was hanging from somewhere. Inside the skull? Behind the heart? Some other place?

My mind was putting the load on. My limbs were left to creak under it.

I would fight Ichijou Ayane.
That intention had weight.

The girl had declared that she would not forgive Kageaki Minato. All the sins he had committed—she would not forgive those.

Condemnation.

The accused, meaning myself, had no objection. Correct. These sins were beyond forgiveness.

They must not be forgiven.

Then why was I required to resist?

Was resistance even permitted to me?

No. It should not be.

If I remembered the lives these hands had taken, the flowers of blood these fingers had brought into bloom...

What business did I have opposing the judgment?

Accept it, na.

If I agreed that the condemnation was just, should I not place myself beneath the executioner's blade?

Yes. That was how it ought to go.

Until now, nobody had come to judge me. I had escaped notice, that was all.

Now somebody had come, carrying scales and sickle: judge and executioner together.

Then—

付近を潜行する劒冑から送られてくる、無言の視線
が煩わしい。
　それでも黙殺して、立ち上がる。

　慣れ親しむ肉体は、<ruby>矢鱈<rt>やたら</rt></ruby>と重かった。
　気を緩めれば膝が笑い出す程に。

　体重ではない重みが何処かに懸かっているようでも
ある。
　何処か――頭蓋の中か、心臓の奥か、それ以外か。

　<ruby>精神<rt>こころ</rt></ruby>が負荷を掛けている。
　四肢に軋みを上げさせている。

　綾弥一条と戦う。
　その意思が、重い。

　あの少女は許さないと宣言したのだ。
　湊斗景明を――彼が犯してきた罪業を。許さないと
告げたのだ。

　断罪。

　<ruby>被告<rt>おれ</rt></ruby>は、同意する。
　その通り――到底、許されざる罪だ。

　許されてはならない罪だ。

　ならば、どうして……
　俺は抗わねばならないのか。

　抗うなどという真似が、許されるのか。

　否。
　許されない筈だ。

　この手で剥奪した命を、
　この指で咲かせた血華を、

　忘れないのならば……
　どうして、裁きに抗おう。

　受け入れるべきではないのか。

　<ruby>断罪<rt>さばき</rt></ruby>の正当を認めるならば、
　刑吏の刃に身を委ねるべきではないのか……

　そう。
　それが、当然の筈だ。

　今までは俺を裁く者が現れなかっただけだ。
　見逃されてきただけだ。

　今はいる。
　天秤と鎌を持つ、判事にして処刑人たる者が訪れて
いる。

　ならば――

en.html:
Again the same argument. Round completed, please begin again.

I was not permitted to escape into relief. Admit my guilt, accept the sentence, surrender this one life—and I could be at ease. But not yet.

First complete the mission. Only afterward would I have the right.

I knew this.
I knew it.

But then came the other thought. Was I not using this very thing to escape my guilt?

Everybody had work left to do. Every living being had something to accomplish while alive. This was not a special facility issued to Kageaki Minato.

Nobody could remain immortal. Everybody died with things unfinished.

So, "I have a mission"—did that amount to a valid reason to avoid death?

It did not.

Like all the dead in this world, like those people I had killed and suddenly robbed of their futures, should I not die here too, struggling and suffering with all my regrets intact?

Would that not be the correct conclusion...?

ja.html:
問答の繰り返し。

　俺に、安逸への逃避は許されない。
　罪を認め、刑に服し、一命を捧げれば楽になれよう
――だが、まだその時ではない。

　使命を果たし終えた後でなくては、俺にはそうする
資格が無い。

　わかっているのだ。
　わかっているのだ。

　しかし――思う。
　それは、罪からの逃避ではないのかと。

　やらねばならぬ事があるのは誰も同じだ。
　生きとし生けるもの全てが、生きて果たすべき使命
を持っている。

　しかし誰もが不死ではいられない。
　誰もが未練を抱えて死んでゆく。

　そう思えば、使命など、死を避けるに値する理由と
言えようか。
　言えまい。

　この世のあらゆる死者のように――俺に殺され不意
に未来を奪われた人々のように、
　俺もまた無念を抱え、ここでもがき苦しんで死んで
ゆくべきではないのか。

　それこそが正しい帰結ではないのか……

en.html:
No need to tell me. If I abandoned the mission given to me, it would not stop at losing my one life. The Silver Star would keep killing. Keep driving people mad, spreading its 'eggs,' raising more copies of itself.

History would put down its name as a calamity without precedent. That, I could not allow.

I had to stop it. Immense damage was already done. At least the line of victims must not be allowed to grow any longer.

...But for that, today, I had to fight Ichijou Ayane.

Her condemnation was just. I had to reject it. Defeat her, trample over her, and keep going. That was what I had to do.
en.text:
No need to tell me. If I abandoned the mission given to me, it would not stop at losing my one life. The Silver Star would keep killing. Keep driving people mad, spreading its 'eggs,' raising more copies of itself.

History would put down its name as a calamity without precedent. That, I could not allow.

I had to stop it. Immense damage was already done. At least the line of victims must not be allowed to grow any longer.

...But for that, today, I had to fight Ichijou Ayane.

Her condemnation was just. I had to reject it. Defeat her, trample over her, and keep going. That was what I had to do.
